name: Reformation
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $128 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's dresses, tops, knitwear, denim, shoes and bags in lower-impact fabrics, dresses around $150–$350, sold through its own stores and site and through Nordstrom.
origin: Founded in Los Angeles, United States in 2009 by Yael Aflalo.

quote.q: I founded Reformation with the vision of creating a brand that appeals to fashionable consumers, but doesn’t destroy the planet
quote.who: Yael Aflalo, founder and then chief executive

opview: “I founded Reformation with the vision of creating a brand that appeals to fashionable consumers, but doesn’t destroy the planet” — Yael Aflalo, founder and then chief executive, City A.M.

facts_read.source: brand site (About, Careers); Permira portfolio page; City A.M. 2019-07-11; FashionNetwork 2019-07-11; nordstrom.com; Vinted catalog page; TRR designer directory; B Lab directory; GOTS database

Jeans.hp: Cary High Rise Slouchy Straight Leg Jeans

price_read.sublines: Reformation incl. Ref Jeans and Ref shoes. EXCLUDED: Veda (leather sister label sold on the site) and stocked brands (Patagonia, Barbour).

doors.note: site thereformation.com (/stores is a 404; the locator is /stores.html); 64 US rows: 62 open stores incl. Melrose Vintage, and 2 marked COMING SOON (Corte Madera, Country Club Plaza) with no address on their pages (status opening, street 'not stated by locator'); no outlets or concessions; Scottsdale's page path says pop-up but nothing on the locator does, kept as own door and flagged; Pacific Palisades page gives no state or ZIP; Houston Galleria gives no ZIP; 4 rows have no phone; store names are the locator's ('Ref Summit')

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 80 of 1,108 seven-digit style codes (colour suffix stripped) read off 11 nodes at sz=1000 (dresses, tops, sweaters, pants, skirts, shorts,

tech_evidence.names: NONE (performance). Licensed fibre brands are sustainability fibres, not technical cloths: TENCEL, LENZING ECOVERO x REFIBRA, Naia Renew, CIRCULOSE, NATIVA
tech_evidence.owned: NONE owned; fibre brands above licensed

craft_evidence.owned: claimed — 'we make all of our stuff with great people at our Los Angeles factory and at our partner factories around the world' (about page); 6 of 76 sampled PDPs say 'made in Los Angeles'. No filing
craft_evidence.makers: yes, as a list, not on the product page — 'we disclose 100% of Tier 1 finished goods manufacturers and subcontractors' (Tier 1 facilities list PDF, August 2026; Open Supply Hub); PDF linked, not opene
craft_evidence.mills: no mills named; cotton named to farm on denim ('Good Earth Cotton from the first climate positive farm in Australia')
craft_evidence.madein: 74 of 76 state a country ('Sustainably made in Mexico'); spread: China, Vietnam, Mexico, Los Angeles/USA (10), Turkey, P
craft_evidence.heritage: dated, not placed: 'Since 2009, we've been on a mission to bring sustainable fashion to everyone'
craft_evidence.process: partly — deadstock buying, vegetable/chrome-free tanning and fibre sourcing are described; garment making is not
craft_evidence.reasoning: Reformation says it makes in its own Los Angeles factory, and 6 of 76 sampled pages say 'made in Los Angeles'; it publishes its full Tier 1 factory list, and 74 of 76 pages state a country. That is named and partly owned making that covers only part of the range. The ownership rests on the brand's own statement: if the Tier 1 PDF does not list an owned LA facility, this is a 3.

notes.tech: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-15): named fabrics NONE (performance). Licensed fibre brands are sustainability fibres, not technical cloths: TENCEL, LENZING ECOVERO x REFIBRA, Naia Renew, CIRCULOSE, NATIVA, 0% (0/76 sampled styles) of the range. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
